source: ECharts 6.1.0 dist (echarts.js) under node, svg painter, ssr init then _ssr = false, env.node = false, TZ=UTC
notes: The clock is reset to T0 per case; setOption steps every clip once at T0 (frame 0); a later frame is T0 + t, one zr.animation.update(), the timers due, getDisplayList(true).
hover is handler.findHover after the event.
name.text is the name as drawn (the tspans after the truncation); name.full the text the element holds.
convert: the parallel coordinate system has no convertToPixel / convertFromPixel; containPixel asks its containPoint.

cases.note: the defaults: horizontal, the box 80 / 60 / 80 / 60, four axes with names, one series of four rows
layout 'vertical': the axes are rows, rotation 0, labels below each line
every axis type: value, category with data, category collected from the data, time (zoned strings and a number), log
a parallelAxis with data and no type is a VALUE axis (the parallel default type wins over the data)
inverse on a value and a category axis: the extent swapped, the name at the other end
min above max: the scale turns round and the axis inverts AFTER its extent was set -- only the name moves
forty categories on a horizontal and on a vertical parallel: the automatic label interval measures along the axis (a quarter turn on the horizontal layout)
min / max, scale: true, splitNumber, interval, dataMin / dataMax
names: start, middle (turned with the axis), end with a gap, nameRotate, one too long for the space between axes, nameTruncate's own maxWidth, a nameTextStyle colour and size

parallelAxis.name: A name far too long to fit between two of these axes at all

name.full: A name far too long to fit between two of these axes at all

cases.note: names on a vertical layout: end, start, middle; a long one cut to the row spacing

parallelAxis.name: A long name on a vertical layout that the row spacing cuts short

name.text: A long name on a vertical layout that the row spacing cuts short
name.full: A long name on a vertical layout that the row spacing cuts short

cases.note: axis labels: rotate 30 and -45, margin 14, a formatter template, showMinLabel false, axisLabel.show false (the coordinate system shows them anyway), an interval on a category axis, inside (ignored)
ticks 9 long and inside (ignored), minor ticks, a hidden axis line, a hidden axis, arrows on the line, a hidden tick
the box as percents, width and height, and a right-and-bottom-only box
parallel.parallelAxisDefault merged under every axis of it (the preprocessor; an axis' own key wins)
the axes in component order, not dim order: dims 3, 0, 2 -- the series maps each row element by its dim
no parallel component: the preprocessor creates one
axisExpandable: eight axes, axisExpandCount 4 about axisExpandCenter 3, axisExpandWidth 60 -- the collapsed axes stand axisCollapseWidth apart, their labels hidden and their names cut to that width
smooth true (0.3), a number, a numeric string, 0 and false; and an empty value dropping its point
empty values: null and NaN on value axes are dropped, a null on a category axis too, an unknown category is not
the palette over three series; lineStyle width 2 dashed and its own colour; item lineStyle colour, width, opacity, type; series color
two parallels side by side, axes and series by parallelIndex (one series names parallelId)
a continuous visualMap on dimension 2 colouring the lines; its opacity channel is overwritten by parallelVisual
a piecewise visualMap on the default dimension (the last), outOfRange grey, seriesIndex picking one series

[R2-I6] a piecewise visualMap's categories on dimension 1, a string column no axis reads (guessOrdinal types it ordinal and the store keeps the text), with another string column before it; a category the list lacks is out of range; a second, continuous visualMap on a numeric column no axis reads (a numeric string is a number)

[r2v] a continuous visualMap on a column no axis reads whose first value is '-': guessOrdinal learns nothing from a dash and goes on to the number after it, so the column is a number and the visualMap colours the rows after it by their numbers (the dash row opted out with visualMap: false)

[r2v] the same column written as text after the dash: a number to guessOrdinal (a numeric string is only a might), so '3.10' is the number 3.1 and '8.0' the number 8 -- the categories '3.1' and '8' take them as String(value) (an ordinal column would keep the text, which neither category equals)
two named series and a legend: the icons; toggling one off rescales the axes
hovering a line: emphasis (the stroke lifted, z2 +10), the item tooltip (the whole row inline), the events; then another line, then leave
emphasis.focus 'series' and its own emphasis / blur lineStyle: the other series blurs

axisAreaSelect: one interval on an axis by id (active 1, inactive 0.05), two intervals, a second axis by index, a reversed interval, clear; an item lineStyle.opacity shows only while nothing is selected
activeOpacity / inactiveOpacity of the series; a selection kept across a setOption merge; the axis named by name
a legend click after a selection keeps the active intervals (they live on the axis model)
the enter animation: the data group clip grows in width over 1000 ms, linear; removed after
vertical: the clip grows in height; animationDuration 600, a delay of 100, two series
an easing of the series' own (cubicOut) and animation off on the second series
containPixel answers on a parallel (its rect), on a parallelAxis (its coordinate system) and on a parallel series; convertToPixel / convertFromPixel answer nothing
containPixel on a vertical parallel with a box of its own, beside a grid
parallelAxis in the baseOption, the parallel series only in the timeline's frames: every frame is preprocessed, so the first one brings the parallel; an axisAreaSelect, then the second frame
the parallel series only in a media unit with a query: the unit is preprocessed and brings the parallel
a merge that brings the parallelAxis and the parallel series beside a grid: the merged option is preprocessed and brings the parallel

guards: the default box is 80 / 60 / 80 / 60
a horizontal axis is turned a quarter, a vertical one not at all
the horizontal transform carries cos(pi/2) into x
the labels sit on the +1 side: left-aligned beside a horizontal layout's axis
a parallelAxis with data and no type is a value axis
a category axis collects its categories from the data
a backwards min and max inverts the axis after its extent was set
the category interval thins forty labels on both layouts
inverse swaps the extent
the end name of an inverse axis is at the other end
a name longer than the space between axes is cut
nameTruncate's own maxWidth cuts with its ellipsis
axisLabel.show false is overruled by the coordinate system
a hidden axis draws nothing
the preprocessor creates a parallel
parallelAxisDefault reaches every axis, the axis wins
the axes follow component order
an expandable layout hides a collapsed axis' labels and cuts its name
smooth true is 0.3
a numeric string smooths
smooth false and 0 draw straight
an empty value drops its point
a null category drops its point, an unknown one not
the default opacity is 0.45
the polyline sits at z2 10
an item's lineStyle opacity wins while nothing is selected
the visualMap colours the stroke
the visualMap's opacity is overwritten
outOfRange greys a row
a category on a string column no axis reads colours its line
a numeric column no axis reads is a number to a continuous visualMap
a numeric text after a dash is a number: the category 3.1 takes 3.10, 8 takes 8.0
a dash first tells guessOrdinal nothing: the numbers after it colour
the legend toggle rescales an axis
a hover lifts the stroke and z2
the item tooltip names the row by its first category and shows the last numeric coordinate
focus series blurs the other series
axisAreaSelect fires axisareaselected then brushselected
active rows are opaque, inactive ones 0.05
an item's own opacity loses to an active state
a reversed interval is sorted
a null value is inactive
an empty list clears
the selection survives a merge
the selection survives a legend toggle
the enter clip starts at 0 width
the enter clip is removed after its end
a vertical clip grows in height
the parallel coordinate system converts nothing
containPixel answers on an axis finder
containPixel answers on a series finder
a timeline frame with the parallel series brings the parallel
the frame's parallel takes the selection
the selection survives the next frame
a media unit with the parallel series brings the parallel
a merge with the parallel series brings the parallel
